passage:
Friday night.

Finally did the thing I kept postponing. I saved ten job listings for the role I want, data analyst, and put them side by side in a spreadsheet. Then I listed every skill they asked for. SQL: nine of ten. A spreadsheet tool: ten of ten. A charting tool: seven. Basic statistics: eight. Storytelling with data: five, though in different words.

Then I marked what I already have. Spreadsheets: yes. Statistics: half. SQL: no. Charting: no. So the gap is clear, and it's smaller than I feared. Anjali says to start with SQL because it's what most listings want. I signed up for a course that begins Monday and put one hour every evening in my diary.

The target has picked my study plan.

Salma

qa.a: Salma could practise the same skill with a small real dataset alongside it, because the target skills are what count and there is more than one way to learn them.

qa.a: Anjali may be pleased that the advice about SQL was taken and that Salma built the plan from evidence and not guesswork.

passage:
In the small town of Kottayam, Joseph worked as an accounts clerk at a rubber cooperative and wanted to become a web developer. For a year he'd bought random online courses and finished none.
One evening at his friend Sahil's phone repair shop, he borrowed a notebook. "I'm going backwards this time," he said. He had printed ten job ads for junior web developers from the district town and the city.
He read them aloud and tallied. "Ten want basic web languages. Eight want one framework. Six want a portfolio site. Four want some database work." Then he wrote what he already had: "Spreadsheets. Some database from the cooperative's stock system. That's it."
Sahil leaned over. "So what's first?"
"The basics, then the framework they all mention, then a portfolio. The database I half have." Joseph crossed out three of the random courses on his phone. "The ads decide. Not me guessing."

qa.q: How many ads wanted a portfolio site?
qa.a: Six ads wanted a portfolio site.

qa.q: What does Joseph's crossing out of courses suggest he is feeling?
qa.a: It suggests he feels clearer and more determined, relieved to stop guessing after a year of unfinished courses.

qa.q: What else could Joseph do with the list of gaps?
qa.a: He could set a rough order and timeframe for each gap and check it with a working developer, so the plan stays realistic.

qa.q: How might Sahil see Joseph's new approach?
qa.a: Sahil seems curious and supportive, asking what comes first and watching his friend finally make a clear plan.

grounding: Shows the person collecting ten job ads, tallying common skills against existing ones and letting the target role shape the study plan.
